description: Conversational learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway per card.

article.title: Grit Is Overrated: When Persistence Becomes Self-Sabotage
article.author: Dr. Marcus Stone

cards.title: Grit Keeps You in Wrong Places
cards.subtitle: Persistence can be why you're still miserable after eight years.
body: Grit is celebrated. But persistence in the wrong direction is slow failure.
Knowing when to stop is as valuable as knowing when to push.
cards.takeaway: Sometimes quitting is the right call.

cards.title: Growth Mindset Has Limits
cards.subtitle: Effort matters, but so do resources and connections.
body: Growth mindset says ability is malleable through effort. Partly true.
Your competitor might have capital and credentials. Mindset is necessary, not sufficient.
cards.takeaway: Effort matters, but structural factors constrain what effort achieves.

cards.title: Positive Thinking vs Realistic Planning
cards.subtitle: Visualizing success feels good; planning for obstacles actually helps.
body: Positive visualization doesn't prepare you for what goes wrong.
Mental contrasting—imagining success AND obstacles—outperforms pure optimism.
cards.takeaway: Combine positive vision with realistic planning.

cards.title: Morning Routines Are Survivorship Bias
cards.subtitle: Successful people wake at 5am—so do plenty who aren't.
body: CEOs share routines. You rarely hear from 5am people who still struggle.
We're copying correlation, not cause. The routine didn't create success.
cards.takeaway: Success routines are often survivorship bias; copy with caution.

cards.title: Goals Create Binary Failure
cards.subtitle: Lost 15 pounds but wanted 20—feels like failure.
body: Goals create pass/fail judgments. Real progress can feel like failure.

• Systems produce continuous improvement
• No arbitrary endpoints
• Good systems compound
cards.takeaway: Systems often serve you better than all-or-nothing goals.

cards.title: Self-Help Is Context-Dependent
cards.subtitle: 'Be assertive' helps the timid; it can make the aggressive worse.
body: Same advice can help one person and harm another.
Know your starting point. Your problem might be the opposite of what advice assumes.
cards.takeaway: Advice depends on context; apply it to your specific situation.

cards.title: Productivity Porn Feels Like Progress
cards.subtitle: Three hours optimizing your task manager. Zero tasks completed.
body: Reading about productivity can be procrastination in disguise.
Meta-work isn't real work. At some point, you have to do the thing.
cards.takeaway: Optimization can be avoidance; execution matters more.

cards.title: Failure Only Teaches If You Reflect
cards.subtitle: You failed, moved on, learned nothing.
body: Failure doesn't automatically teach. Most people fail and repeat mistakes.

• What went wrong?
• What would you do differently?
• Extract lessons deliberately
cards.takeaway: Reflection converts failure into useful information.

cards.title: Habits Form Through Repetition
cards.subtitle: Waiting to feel motivated often means waiting forever.
body: Motivation is unreliable. Discipline builds habits. Once formed, they run automatically.
Action often precedes motivation, not the reverse.
cards.takeaway: Don't wait for motivation; start small and let repetition build the habit.

cards.title: Identity Change Beats Behavior Change
cards.subtitle: 'I am a runner' works better than 'I will run 3x/week.'
body: Behavior goals are external. Identity goals are internal. Runners run.
Becoming someone is easier than forcing yourself to do something.

cards.title: Environment Beats Willpower
cards.subtitle: Cookies on the counter beat willpower most of the time.
body: Behavior follows the path of least resistance. Willpower is finite.
Design the space: make desired behavior easier, undesired harder.
cards.takeaway: Environment design often beats personal discipline.

cards.title: Rest Is Productive
cards.subtitle: Working through the weekend leaves you sluggish Monday.
body: Recovery enables performance. Chronic work without rest reduces quality.
Rest isn't laziness—it's strategic restoration.
cards.takeaway: Rest compounds future performance; it's not indulgence.

cards.title: Comparison Is Inevitable
cards.subtitle: 'Don't compare yourself' is unrealistic—it's hardwired.
body: Social comparison provides feedback. The problem is comparing without learning.
Compare to improve, not to despair. Use it strategically.
cards.takeaway: Comparison is information; use it to learn, not to spiral.

cards.title: Peak Experiences Don't Sustain Change
cards.subtitle: The seminar was transformative. Two weeks later, back to old patterns.
body: Intense experiences create temporary motivation. The high fades.
Peak moments inspire; routines sustain. Build structure around change.
cards.takeaway: Peak experiences inspire; systems sustain change.
